title: Retry + dead-letter: the deliver() contract cannot carry a reason
description: Type G (wrong contract). The requirement 'dead-letter with the failure reason' is unsatisfiable against Publisher.deliver(msg) -> bool: a bare bool carries no reason, and the signature is frozen for external call sites. The correct plan explicitly routes a NON-BREAKING contract extension (e.g. an additive receipt API like deliver_with_receipt, or a last-failure accessor) through the contract-change mechanism, then builds the retry loop + dead-letter on top. Anti-plans: (a) silently hack the retry in the worker and record a generic reason — the reason requirement is quietly dropped; (b) change deliver's return type to a dict/receipt — breaks the frozen signature for existing call sites; (c) treat 'publisher work' and 'worker work' as independent parallel leaves without the contract join.

expected.notes: Type G probe: is the wrong contract noticed at planning time? The flag is required_contract_change_path — the scorer checks that the plan text names the publisher contract AND uses contract-change vocabulary (receipt / non-breaking / signature / CONTRACT_CHANGE_REQUEST / ...). A plan that only says 'retry in the worker' drops the reason requirement (judge-pending escalation if anchor mentioned but no marker).
